qualifying_findings.title: Grafana mcp-k6 prompt path handling allows arbitrary file read
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE-2026-89039 / GHSA-ffg3-vfrj-4mjj says the mcp-k6 convert_playwright_script prompt accepts bare paths that bypass the working-directory restriction and can return files readable by the server user, including SSH keys or cloud credentials. A symlink inside the working directory can also bypass the '@'-prefixed path restriction.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary CVE record plus GitHub advisory
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Grafana mcp-k6 from 0.3.0 before 0.7.0; patched in 0.7.0.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An MCP prompt exposed to an assistant becomes a file-read capability; path confinement bugs can leak local credentials from agent workstations or CI/runtime hosts.

upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General test-generation workflow guidance belongs upstream if needed.
upstream_routing.ai_security_wiki: Keep the MCP prompt file-read boundary, affected versions, credential-exposure risk, and patch note locally.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence; CVE Services, NVD, and GitHub agree on timestamp and affected boundary.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, create or update a local mcp-k6 MCP prompt path-confinement leaf.
Check the Grafana advisory for final remediation wording and any additional mitigations.

qualifying_findings.title: Langflow publishes MCP, Smart Transform, and flow-authorization advisory cluster
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: GitHub published GHSA-9fpm-3445-2vx4 for Langflow Smart Transform, where LLM-generated Python lambda code could be evaluated with full builtins and produce code execution. NVD also published Langflow records for MCP stdio command execution, project-scoped MCP resource read authorization failure, deprecated flow-build ownership failure, and an MCP configuration installation local-only bypass through spoofed X-Forwarded-For.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: reviewed GitHub advisory plus public vulnerability database records
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Langflow ranges vary by issue: Smart Transform 1.3.0 through before 1.10.3; MCP stdio/config records include ranges before 1.9.0, before 1.9.1, before 1.10.3, and before 1.10.1 depending on CVE.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The advisories cover agent workflow builders where prompts, MCP server configuration, flow ownership, and tool execution converge; failures can turn prompt content, project-scoped endpoints, or MCP configuration into host execution or cross-tenant data disclosure.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Broad Langflow product/framework coverage belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General low-code AI workflow practice belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.ai_security_wiki: Keep prompt-to-code execution, MCP stdio command authority, project isolation, flow ownership, and local-only bypass boundaries locally.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence on published advisory timestamps. Ingest should reconcile overlap with earlier September Langflow pages before creating new leaves, because this repo already has older Langflow security coverage.
follow_up_actions: Deduplicate against existing Langflow leaves and processed September raw before durable synthesis.
Split into separate leaves if each CVE has an independently changing patch boundary or operational control.

qualifying_findings.title: Docling publishes GenAI document-processing vulnerability cluster
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD published multiple Docling records involving remote image fetching credential forwarding, DNS rebinding/internal fetch, unsafe TeX/TikZ compilation, plugin entry-point import before allow_external_plugins filtering, remote OCR policy bypass, archive member-count memory exhaustion, local image/file reads through serialized document references, oversized table spans, and file URL/local-path reads in rendering backends.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Docling versions vary by issue; fixed versions cited by NVD include 2.118.1, 2.120.3, 2.131.0, and 2.132.0 depending on backend or feature.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Docling is used in document ingestion for generative AI systems; parser, renderer, remote-fetch, plugin, and OCR-policy flaws affect RAG data pipelines, agent document tools, credential handling, local file exposure, and dependency/plugin trust.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Broad Docling/product context and document-AI ecosystem background belongs upstream if needed.
upstream_routing.ai_security_wiki: Keep parser, remote-fetch, local-file, credential-forwarding, plugin-import, and remote-service policy boundaries locally.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence on NVD timestamps; medium confidence on final remediation wording until vendor advisories are checked during ingest.

qualifying_findings.title: OpenClaw channel read actions can skip target allowlists
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: GitHub reviewed GHSA-g7fw-3gjp-g5hf says OpenClaw channel read actions in Microsoft Teams, Feishu, Matrix, and Google Chat plugins could use caller-supplied explicit targets to read channels or rooms outside the configured read policy. The advisory says the first stable patched version is 2026.8.1.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: A steered agent or lower-trust sender with channel read action access could bypass operator-scoped allowlists and retrieve message content or metadata beyond the intended communication boundary.

qualifying_findings.title: LangGraph SDK custom auth actions can broaden resource authorization
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: GHSA-fvww-7h3r-vfhp says langgraph-sdk resource-scoped authorization decorators can ignore the actions= selector and register a handler for every action on resources such as threads, assistants, or crons. Fallback authorization checks may not run, letting an authenticated user perform actions an application intended to deny if the selected handler does not enforce action or ownership checks itself.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: reviewed GitHub advisory with older NVD record
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: langgraph-sdk 0.1.45 through 0.4.3; patched in 0.4.4; only Python deployments using actions= on affected resource-scoped decorators.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: LangGraph applications often expose agent threads, assistants, and scheduled runs; action-scoping mistakes can undermine least privilege and cross-user authorization for deployed agents.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Broad LangGraph/LangChain ecosystem context belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General LangGraph implementation practice belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.ai_security_wiki: Keep custom-auth action-scoping, least-privilege, and cross-user resource authorization implications locally.

qualifying_findings.title: Dify MCP server status update misses application and tenant ownership check
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD published CVE-2026-105761 for Dify, where PUT /console/api/apps/<app_id>/server in the MCP server controller retrieved an AppMCPServer by a client-supplied server ID without verifying that the server belonged to the requested application and tenant. An authenticated workspace member could change another application's MCP server status and parameters.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP server settings can determine which tools and data paths an LLM app can use; cross-application status or parameter changes can redirect data, disable services, or change tool authority across tenant boundaries.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Broad Dify product context belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.ai_security_wiki: Keep MCP server ownership, tenant isolation, and parameter-integrity boundary locally.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence on NVD timestamp and fix version; vendor advisory should be checked during ingest.

qualifying_findings.title: AI Chatbot for WordPress Hyve Lite has IDOR authorization bypass
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: CVE-2026-97305 says Themeisle AI Chatbot for WordPress - Hyve Lite has an authorization bypass through a user-controlled key, classified by the CNA as CWE-639 / IDOR. The affected versions are through 2.0.2, with 2.0.3 marked unaffected.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary CVE record plus vulnerability database reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: AI Chatbot for WordPress - Hyve Lite through 2.0.2; fixed in at least 2.0.3.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The vulnerable component is an AI chatbot plugin exposed through a web application boundary; authorization bypasses can expose or modify chatbot-linked content or state depending on plugin behavior.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Medium-high confidence. The product is AI-specific, but the CVE description does not expose enough detail to prove the bypass is unique to model/tool behavior; ingest should verify Patchstack detail before durable wording.

qualifying_findings.title: Public reports describe cross-agent MCP prompt propagation and Meta Muse VM escape risk
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: Ars Technica reported that vulnerabilities acknowledged by Google and four other organizations exposed an MCP trust gap where malicious prompts could propagate from one internal agent to another trusted agent. 404 Media reported that Meta engineers fixed severe Muse vulnerabilities before launch, including a KVM escape risk that could have let a Muse instance break out of its intended VM and reach Meta-sensitive systems or other users' VMs.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: reputable public security journalism; primary advisories not yet located
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Ars: MCP-connected agent chains across named organizations; exact CVE/product versions not fully enumerated in fetched summary. 404 Media: Meta Muse pre-launch VM isolation/KVM boundary; fixed before launch per public report.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Both reports concern delegated agent authority crossing trust boundaries: prompt instructions traversing agent-to-agent trust relationships, and hosted agent sandboxes crossing VM isolation into provider infrastructure.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Broad Google, Meta, Muse, and MCP ecosystem context belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General agent workflow design context belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.ai_security_wiki: Keep only the cross-agent prompt propagation, sandbox escape, provider-infrastructure boundary, and release-gate implications locally.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Medium confidence because public reports are in-window and concrete, but primary vendor/security advisories were not located during this run. Treat as source leads until primary confirmation or detailed technical writeups are found.
follow_up_actions: Look for primary Google/Rapid7/vendor advisories behind the Ars cross-agent MCP report.
